candidates.story_title: Alaska enacts HB 239, criminalizing AI-generated CSAM as a felony; became law without governor's signature ~June 19-20
key_claims: HB 239 is an omnibus crime bill combining provisions from ~10 bills.
It criminalizes AI-generated child sexual abuse material as a Class B felony (Class A for repeat), possession as Class C felony.
Passed Senate 20-0 and House 39-1 on May 19-20, 2026.
Became law without Governor Dunleavy's signature around June 19-20, 2026 when the gubernatorial action deadline elapsed.
Dunleavy vetoed 9 other bills June 18 but did not veto HB 239.
candidates.industry_consequence: Digital platform, cloud, and generative-AI operators serving Alaska users face a new state felony framework requiring updated detection/moderation for AI-generated CSAM or risk criminal referral.

candidates.story_title: Saving the OOI Act (S.4822) passes Senate by voice vote June 17; NSF halts OOI decommission by June 19 after Murkowski-led pushback
key_claims: Sen. Murkowski (R-AK) and Sen. Merkley (D-OR) introduced S.4822 on June 17, 2026.
It passed the full Senate by voice vote.
NSF committed to halt removal/descoping of the ~900-instrument OOI array, including Gulf of Alaska instruments, by June 18-19.
OOI data feeds NOAA/UAF fisheries stock assessments supporting Alaska's commercial seafood industry.
candidates.industry_consequence: Alaska fisheries managers and seafood operators retain the real-time ocean data underpinning catch-limit science; risk deferred pending NSF expert-panel review.

State Rep. Genevieve Mina said the federal program is 'almost directing us to AI.'
